title: Cuatro Leches Cake
subtitle: Original recipe by Dunia Borga, co-owner and pastry chef, La Duni Latin Café
headnote: The original La Duni Cuatro Leches: vanilla mantecada sponge layered with three-milk soak, covered in caramelized meringue, and finished with arequipe sauce. Transcribed from the original restaurant recipe published in 2012.
sourceNote: La Duni Latin Café, cuatrolechescakeweb.pdf, V.02.10.03 BIC 2003; original by pastry chef Dunia Borga.

ingredientGroups.title: Vanilla mantecada cake (original)
items: Butter and parchment for one 8-inch cake pan

ingredientGroups.title: Dulce de leche
items: 1 can sweetened condensed milk, for making dulce de leche (or 1 cup prepared dulce de leche; safer substitute)

ingredientGroups.title: Assembly
items: 1 cup three-milk sauce, listed for assembly (source's detailed method calls for more)

steps.heading: Vanilla mantecada cake — La Duni PDF

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Sift flour, baking powder and salt together.
Cream the butter until very fluffy using a stand mixer with a paddle. Gradually beat in the sugar; add eggs individually on low speed. Mix in the vanilla.
Add a third of the flour mixture, then half the milk; alternate with the remaining flour and milk, ending with flour. Mix briefly, approximately 1 minute or less, and avoid overmixing.
Pour into a buttered, parchment-lined 8-inch round cake pan. Bake on the lower third rack for 55–70 minutes, until the center springs back and the sides pull away. Cool completely.
The original recipe instructs simmering a sealed can of condensed milk in water for 2 hours. For safety, substitute 1 cup prepared dulce de leche instead.
Whisk evaporated milk, condensed milk and cream until combined; refrigerate. Separately whisk the dulce de leche with warmed whole milk for the arequipe sauce and refrigerate.

Heat the sugar and water to 240°F (soft-ball stage). Beat egg whites to soft peaks; while beating at medium speed, carefully drizzle in the hot syrup. Beat at high speed with the lemon juice and vanilla to stiff peaks.
Remove the cake from its parchment and slice horizontally into three even layers. Prick each layer with a fork.

Brush with the three-milk mixture while stacking layers. The original recipe lists 1 cup in its assembly ingredients but directs 6 oz per layer (18 oz total); check the desired saturation before pouring and do not assume the figures agree.

Cover the cake with approximately ½-inch of meringue, making peaks with a spatula. Torch until golden; drizzle with arequipe and dust with powdered sugar. Serve with additional milk sauce and caramel.
reviewFlags: Original PDF cake formula uses ONE 8-inch pan and 55–70 minutes; this differs materially from CraftyBaking's two 9-inch layers and ~40 minutes.
Original PDF lists 1 cup of three-milk sauce for assembly but instructs brushing 6 oz on each of three layers. These amounts are inconsistent; original values are retained.
The original PDF calls its hot-syrup topping 'Caramelized Meringue'; this preparation is Italian-style meringue, not a conventional uncooked Swiss meringue.
Sealed-can simmering for dulce de leche in the PDF is replaced in directions with safer prepared dulce de leche; original method is described in the note.

variants.title: Cuatro Leches Cake
variants.subtitle: Updated by CraftyBaking
variants.yield: Two 9-inch cake layers, assembled as one tall cake
variants.headnote: CraftyBaking's tested revision of chef Dunia Borga's La Duni cake. The cake batter and procedures are revised, sauce proportions are smaller, and two baked layers are each split for assembly.
variants.sourceNote: CraftyBaking, Sarah Phillips, 'Cuatro Leches Vanilla Mantecado Cake' (2011); revised from chef Dunia Borga's La Duni original.

ingredientGroups.title: Vanilla mantecada layers
items: 375 g all-purpose flour (3 cups, spooned and leveled)
Parchment and butter for two 9-inch pans

ingredientGroups.title: Dulce de leche and arequipe
items: 1 cup prepared dulce de leche (about 300 g, brand-dependent)

ingredientGroups.title: Assembly
items: Three-milk soak, about 6 oz for each split cake pair per revised method

steps: Heat oven to 350°F with rack in lower third. Grease two light-colored 9-inch pans and line with parchment. Reduce heat 25°F if using dark nonstick or glass pans.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt. Stir vanilla into the milk.
Beat cold butter with a paddle on low until softened, about 60 seconds. Add sugar steadily, beat on medium for 2 minutes until fluffy and scrape bowl.
On low, add eggs one by one, beating 20 seconds after each. Increase to medium and beat 2 minutes.
With mixer on low, alternate flour mixture in three portions with milk in two portions, starting and ending with flour. Scrape the bowl and beat 30 more seconds on low; avoid overmixing.
Divide between prepared pans; bake about 40 minutes in 9-inch pans (about 45 minutes in 8-inch pans). Cool in pans on racks.
Use prepared dulce de leche (or the original CraftyBaking crockpot method if appropriate for your equipment). Whisk with 121 g warm milk for arequipe, then chill.
Whisk the evaporated milk, condensed milk and cream for the three-milk soak, then refrigerate.
Heat sugar and water to 240°F without stirring once boiling; brush down crystals. Whip egg whites to soft peaks.
Slowly pour syrup down side of mixer bowl on medium; beat on high with lemon juice and vanilla until firm peaks. Use immediately.
Turn both cooled cakes out and remove parchment. Horizontally split each into two layers. Prick cut surfaces with a fork.
Brush about 6 oz total three-milk sauce onto each split pair. Re-stack the first pair; add a meringue border and filling, then stack the second split pair as described by CraftyBaking.
Cover the cake with a roughly ½-inch meringue coat, pipe decorative borders and torch lightly until golden. Alternatively brown at 450°F for 4–6 minutes, watching continuously.
Drizzle with arequipe, dust with powdered sugar, chill about an hour, and serve with extra sauce. Refrigerate leftovers (CraftyBaking suggests up to 3–4 days).
reviewFlags: CraftyBaking cake formula yields TWO 9-inch layers, yet its assembly ingredient line still mentions ONE 8-inch cake; this entry follows the expanded two-cake assembly instructions and flags that inconsistency.
CraftyBaking's assembly instructs about 6 oz soak per split pair despite a 1 cup sauce line in the ingredient summary; use the expanded assembly amounts with judgment.
Prepared dulce de leche is used as a safer ready-made option; CraftyBaking also documents a sealed-can slow-cooker method.

variants.title: Panque de Limón — Lemon-Curd Variation
variants.subtitle: La Duni lemon variation · complete home rendition
variants.headnote: CraftyBaking describes chef Dunia Borga's Panque de Limón as mantecada cake layered with fresh lemon curd, topped with caramelized meringue and candied lemon peel, and served with raspberry purée. The source gives no quantities for those three added elements; this complete home rendition uses independently attributed supplemental recipes and quantities. This version does NOT use the three-milk soak or arequipe.
variants.sourceNote: Cake and meringue from CraftyBaking (Sarah Phillips); composition of Panque de Limón attributed there to chef Dunia Borga. Supplemental lemon curd from King Arthur Baking (Sarah Jampel, updated 2026), candied lemon peel adapted from Whole Foods Market, and raspberry coulis from BBC Good Food (Esther Clark).

supplementalSources.attribution: Whole Foods Market; scaled down from published batch

ingredientGroups.title: Fresh lemon curd — King Arthur Baking
Candied lemon peel — small batch based on Whole Foods
items: Peel of 2 unwaxed lemons, cut into narrow strips
250 g granulated sugar (200 g syrup plus 50 g coating)
180 g water for syrup, plus extra blanching water

ingredientGroups.title: Raspberry purée — BBC Good Food
items: 450 g fresh or thawed frozen raspberries

steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Grease and line two light-colored 9-inch pans. Sift flour, baking powder and salt; combine milk and vanilla.
Beat butter until softened; add sugar and beat 2 minutes. Beat in eggs one at a time, 20 seconds each, then beat 2 minutes at medium speed.
Alternate flour in three additions with milk in two, mixing on low and ending with flour. Beat 30 seconds on low, then divide between pans.
Bake approximately 40 minutes until centers spring back. Cool in pans, then unmold and remove parchment.

steps.heading: Lemon curd — supplemental King Arthur Baking

steps: Rub lemon zest into sugar until aromatic. Warm the lemon juice in a heavy pan without boiling. Whisk eggs and yolks, gradually whisk in lemon sugar.
Slowly temper egg mixture with warm lemon juice, return to saucepan and whisk continuously over medium heat until it reaches 170°F and thickens (about 6–8 minutes).
Immediately strain, whisk in cold butter, vanilla and salt. Cover surface directly and chill until firmly set, approximately 4 hours. Makes about 730 g.
Peel two washed, unwaxed lemons without much white pith; cut peel into thin strips. Cover with water, bring to boil 1 minute and drain. Repeat twice more.

Simmer the blanched peel in a syrup of 200 g sugar and 180 g water for roughly 45–60 minutes until translucent. Lift out, coat with the remaining 50 g sugar and dry on a rack until no longer tacky. This is a scaled-down variation of the cited Whole Foods recipe.

steps.heading: Raspberry purée — supplemental BBC Good Food

steps: Blend raspberries with lemon juice and icing sugar just until smooth. Pass through a fine sieve to remove seeds. Chill until serving.
Boil 400 g sugar with 118 g water to 240°F. Beat egg whites to soft peaks, gradually stream in syrup while whipping, then beat in lemon juice and vanilla to firm glossy peaks. Use immediately.
Split each cooled mantecada layer horizontally to make four thin layers. Spread chilled lemon curd between the cake layers, reserving a little for the top if desired.
Coat exterior with caramelized meringue, create swoops and peaks, and torch golden. Top with candied lemon peel. Chill until set.
Serve slices with raspberry purée spooned onto the plate. Keep the assembled cake refrigerated and consume within 2–3 days for best texture.
reviewFlags: Panque de Limón on CraftyBaking is an overview, not a complete quantified formula. Curd, peel, raspberry components and assembly choices here are supplementary home-developed instructions, NOT Chef Dunia's authenticated formula.
Supplemental lemon curd from King Arthur Baking was updated in 2026; this component may differ from that used by La Duni historically.
The candied-peel quantity was scaled from the Whole Foods recipe and is therefore an adaptation rather than a reproduction.
This lemon version is not soaked in three-milk sauce and does not use arequipe; its flavor and structure are distinct from Cuatro Leches.
